questions.question:
Use ΔHf°[NH3(g)] = -46 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔHf°[HCl(g)] = -92 kJ mol⁻¹ to calculate ΔHr for the reaction:

3Cl2(g) + 2NH3(g) → N2(g) + 6HCl(g)
steps: Step 1: Pure elements in their standard states (Cl2 and N2) have ΔHf° = 0 kJ mol⁻¹.
Step 2: Apply ΔHr = ΣΔHf°(products) - ΣΔHf°(reactants) = [6 × (-92)] - [2 × (-46)] = -552 + 92 = -460 kJ mol⁻¹.
questions.examinerReport: Candidates frequently divided -460 by 3 thinking enthalpy of reaction had to be per mole of Cl2. Always calculate ΔHr for the exact balanced equation given.

questions.question:
A 5.00 dm³ sealed vessel contains 0.400 mol of CO(g) and 0.800 mol of H2(g) at 290 °C. At equilibrium, 0.280 mol of CH3OH(g) is present:

CO(g) + 2H2(g) ⇌ CH3OH(g)

Calculate Kc at 290 °C to three significant figures and state its units.
steps: Step 2 (Convert to Concentration using V = 5.00 dm³): [CO] = 0.0240, [H2] = 0.0480, [CH3OH] = 0.0560 mol dm⁻³.
Step 3 (Substitute into Kc): Kc = 0.0560 / (0.0240 × 0.0480²) = 1.01 × 10³ mol⁻² dm⁶.
markScheme: M1: Equilibrium moles n(CO) = 0.120 and n(H2) = 0.240 [1]
M2: Dividing all three mole values by 5.00 dm³ [1]
M3: Kc = 1.01 × 10³ AND units mol⁻² dm⁶ [1]
questions.examinerReport: Two common errors occurred: forgetting to divide equilibrium moles by the 5.00 dm³ volume, and subtracting 0.280 instead of 2 × 0.280 for H2.

questions.question: Which electronic configuration represents an isolated gaseous atom with the largest drop between its third and fourth ionisation energies?
steps: Step 1: A large jump between the 3rd and 4th ionisation energies indicates 3 valence electrons in the outer shell (Group 13).
Step 2: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p¹ (Al) has 3 electrons in the n = 3 shell; removing the 4th electron breaks into the inner 2p subshell.
questions.examinerReport: Many candidates confused Group 13 (jump after 3rd IE) with Group 14 (jump after 4th IE).
